chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud from his father who said: We were narrated by Muhammad ibn al-Sindi from Ahmad ibn Idris from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Naysaburi from Abdullah ibn Musa from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Wassha who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying:

"Indeed, for every Imam there is a covenant upon the neck of his allies and his Shia, and among the completion of fulfilling the covenant and good performance is the visiting of their graves. So whoever visits them with desire for their visitation and affirmation of what they desired, their Imams will be their intercessors on the Day of Resurrection."
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of visiting the Imams' graves in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes that visiting the graves of the Imams is not merely a ritual but a crucial component of fulfilling the 'covenant' (‘ahd) inherent in the bond of Wilayah. He clarifies that the requisite sincerity involves both a desire for the visitation itself and an affirmation of the Imams' teachings, thereby securing their intercession (shafa'ah) on the Day of Judgment. This links the physical act of Ziyarah directly to the spiritual status of being among the 'Auliya' (allies) of the Imam.
